अगले 4 से 5 दिनों में न्यूनतम तापमान 2 से 3 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक गिरने की संभावना है। सुबह और रात में ठंड बढ़ेगी।

Maharashtra Weather Update: दिवाली के बाद महाराष्ट्र के मौसम में बड़ा बदलाव देखने को मिल रहा है। भारत मौसम विज्ञान विभाग और क्षेत्रीय मौसम विज्ञान केंद्र, मुंबई के मुताबिक, राज्य के ज़्यादातर हिस्सों से बारिश पूरी तरह खत्म हो गई है और अगले कुछ दिनों तक मौसम सूखा रहेगा।
11 नवंबर को राज्य के किसी भी जिले के लिए बारिश का येलो, ऑरेंज या रेड अलर्ट जारी नहीं किया गया है। इस बीच, अगले 4 से 5 दिनों में मिनिमम टेम्परेचर में 2 से 3 डिग्री सेल्सियस की गिरावट आने की संभावना है। इससे सुबह और रात में ठंड का एहसास होगा। हालांकि, दोपहर में सूरज की तपिश जारी रहेगी।

पुणे में मैक्सिमम टेम्परेचर 32 डिग्री, जबकि मिनिमम टेम्परेचर 15 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने की उम्मीद है। इस वजह से सुबह और रात में ओले पड़ सकते हैं। सतारा, सांगली, कोल्हापुर और अहिल्यानगर जिलों में भी बारिश की कोई संभावना नहीं है और मौसम सूखा रहेगा।
अगले कुछ दिनों तक नागपुर समेत पूरे विदर्भ में बारिश की कोई संभावना नहीं है। नागपुर में अधिकतम तापमान 30 से 34 डिग्री तक बढ़ने की उम्मीद है। अमरावती, अकोला, वर्धा, भंडारा, गोंदिया, चंद्रपुर और गड़चिरोली जिलों में भी मौसम सूखा रहेगा। इससे किसानों को फसल काटने और सुखाने के लिए अच्छा माहौल मिलेगा।
नासिक में दिन में मौसम गर्म रहेगा और रात में हल्की बूंदाबांदी होगी। मराठवाड़ा के छत्रपति संभाजीनगर, जालना, बीड, लातूर, धाराशिव, परभणी, हिंगोली और नांदेड़ जिलों में बारिश की कोई चेतावनी जारी नहीं की गई है। कुल मिलाकर, राज्य में बारिश रुक गई है और तापमान में उतार-चढ़ाव जारी रहेगा। इस वजह से, लोगों को सुबह और रात में ठंड और दोपहर में गर्मी का सामना करना पड़ सकता है।

विस्तार
उत्तर प्रदेश में मौसम अब सर्दियों की ओर बढ़ रहा है। सुबह कोहरा और रात में गिरता तापमान ठंड बढ़ने का संकेत देने लगा है। मंगलवार को तराई, अवध और पूर्वी यूपी के कई जिलों में सुबह हल्का कोहरा छाया रहा। वहीं दिन चढ़ने के साथ धूप निकलने से राहत बनी रही।
मौसम विभाग का कहना है कि बुधवार से कोहरे में कमी आएगी। साथ ही फिलहाल अगले पांच दिन, दिन व रात के पारे में किसी खास बदलाव की संभावना नहीं है। सुबह शाम और रात के मौसम में यूं ही नरमी बनी रहेगी।
उधर दीपावली के अगले दिन सोमवार सुबह पश्चिमी तराई, अवध और पूर्वांचल के कई जिलों में कोहरा छाया रहा। कुछ स्थानों पर इसकी सघनता इतनी अधिक रही कि दृश्यता काफी कम हो गई। वाराणसी में घने कोहरे के कारण दृश्यता शून्य तक पहुंच गई, जबकि बरेली में यह महज 100 मीटर दर्ज की गई। राजधानी लखनऊ में भी सुबह दृश्यता घटकर 300 मीटर रह गई।
क्षेत्रीय मौसम विज्ञान केंद्र लखनऊ के वरिष्ठ वैज्ञानिक अतुल कुमार सिंह ने बताया कि अगले पांच दिन बाद पछुआ हवा रफ्तार पकड़ेगी और इसके असर से ठंड में इजाफा होगा। अगले पांच दिनों तक प्रदेश में कहीं भी बारिश की संभावना नहीं जताई है।
सात जिलों में 15 डिग्री के आसपास पहुंचा रात का पारा
सोमवार और मंगलवार के बीच की रात प्रदेश के करीब सात जिलों में न्यूनतम तापमान 15 डिग्री सेल्सियस के आसपास दर्ज किया गया। हरदोई में पारा गिरकर 13.5 डिग्री सेल्सियस पर पहुंच गया, जो प्रदेश में सबसे कम रहा। वहीं 28 डिग्री सेल्सियस अधिकतम तापमान के साथ इटावा में सबसे ठंडा दिन रहा।

पठानकोट में न्यूनतम तापमान 11.3 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंच गया, जो राज्य में सबसे कम रहा। वहीं, चंडीगढ़ में भी रात का तापमान 13.5 डिग्री दर्ज किया गया। मौसम में बदलाव के साथ लोगों को सुबह घर से निकलते समय हल्की ठंड का सामना करना पड़ रहा है। आने वाले दिनों में बारिश की संभावना के कारण मौसम का मिजाज कुछ और बदल सकता है। मौसम विभाग के मुताबिक, पहाड़ी इलाकों में पश्चिमी विक्षोभ सक्रिय है। इसके अलावा उत्तरी हरियाणा और आसपास के क्षेत्रों में हवा का चक्रवाती सिस्टम बना हुआ है। इन दोनों मौसमी प्रणालियों के प्रभाव से पंजाब के कुछ हिस्सों में बारिश होने की संभावना बन रही है। हालांकि, अगले पांच दिनों के दौरान अधिकतम और न्यूनतम तापमान में किसी बड़े बदलाव का पूर्वानुमान नहीं है।
पठानकोट में सबसे ज्यादा ठंड

चंडीगढ़ में भी गिरा रात का पारा, 13.5 डिग्री तापमान

अलवर जिले में नवंबर के दूसरे सप्ताह में मौसम का मिजाज सामान्य से अलग रहा है। शहर में दोपहर के समय तेज धूप के कारण तापमान 30 डिग्री के आसपाब बना हुआ है। वहीं सुबह और रात के समय हल्की ठंड महसूस हो रही है। सूखी घास पर ओस की बूंदें नजर आ रही हैं।
नवंबर में तापमान का उतार चढ़ाव
राजस्थान मौसम विभाग द्वारा जारी पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार अलवर में तापमान में उतार-चढ़ाव देखने को मिलेगा। 11 और 12 नवंबर को अधिकतम तापमान 30 डिग्री और न्यूनतम 14 डिग्री रहने की संभावना है। मौसम विशेषज्ञों के अनुसार 13 नवंबर को अधिकतम तापमान गिरकर 28 डिग्री तक पहुंच सकता है।

साफ आसमान में बढ़ता प्रदूषण
मौसम विभाग के अनुसार बारिश नहीं होगी और आसमान साफ रहेगा। हालांकि शहर की हवा में प्रदूषण का स्तर चिंताजनक बना हुआ है। बुधवार सुबह 9:01 बजे AQI वेबसाइट पर अलवर का एयर क्वालिटी इंडेक्स 267 दर्ज किया गया। वेबसाइट ने इसे गंभीर श्रेणी में दिखाया।
प्रदूषण के मुख्य कारण PM2.5 और PM10 हैं। इस दौरान PM2.5 का स्तर 192 माइक्रोग्राम प्रति घन मीटर दर्ज किया गया। वहीं PM10 का स्तर 230 माइक्रोग्राम प्रति घन मीटर रहा। यानी हवा में बारीक धूल और प्रदूषण के कणों की मौजूदगी बनी हुई है। मौसम साफ होने के बावजूद ये कण हवा में बरकरार हैं।
जनता पर प्रदूषण का असर
अलवर के निवासियों को प्रदूषण के बढ़ते स्तर से स्वास्थ्य संबंधी समस्याएं हो सकती हैं। गंभीर श्रेणी में AQI होने पर नाजुक स्वास्थ्य वाले लोगों को सावधानी बरतनी चाहिए। हवा में मौजूद धूल और कण फेफड़ों के लिए हानिकारक हैं। स्थानीय लोग इस बात से परेशान हैं कि मौसम बदलने के बावजूद हवा साफ नहीं हो रही है।

गिरने लगा पारा, बढ़ने लगी ठंड! पंजाब के कई शहरों में न्यूनतम तापमान में गिरावट
मौसम में आ रहे बदलाव के पीछे पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में सक्रिय पश्चिमी विक्षोभ को अहम कारण माना जा रहा है। इसके साथ ही उत्तरी हरियाणा और आसपास के इलाकों में चक्रवाती हवा का क्षेत्र भी बना हुआ है।
खबर सुनें
चंडीगढ़। पंजाब और चंडीगढ़ में अब धीरे-धीरे सर्दी का असर महसूस होने लगा है। रातें ठंडी होने के साथ ही राज्य के कई शहरों में न्यूनतम तापमान में गिरावट दर्ज की गई है। मौसम विभाग के पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक, बुधवार को मौसम शुष्क रहेगा, जबकि 12 नवंबर से कुछ इलाकों में बारिश होने की संभावना है। फिलहाल अगले पांच दिनों के दौरान तापमान में किसी बड़े बदलाव के संकेत नहीं हैं।
औसत न्यूनतम तापमान में 1.1 डिग्री की गिरावट
पंजाब के औसत न्यूनतम तापमान में पिछले समय की तुलना में 1.1 डिग्री सेल्सियस की गिरावट दर्ज की गई है। हालांकि, तापमान अभी भी सामान्य स्तर के आसपास बना हुआ है। पठानकोट में पारा सबसे नीचे 11.3 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंच गया। यह राज्य में दर्ज किया गया सबसे कम न्यूनतम तापमान रहा।
पश्चिमी विक्षोभ बदल सकता है मौसम का मिजाज
मौसम में आ रहे बदलाव के पीछे पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में सक्रिय पश्चिमी विक्षोभ को अहम कारण माना जा रहा है। इसके साथ ही उत्तरी हरियाणा और आसपास के इलाकों में चक्रवाती हवा का क्षेत्र भी बना हुआ है। इन दोनों मौसमी प्रणालियों के प्रभाव से 12 नवंबर से पंजाब के कुछ हिस्सों में बारिश हो सकती है। बारिश के कारण स्थानीय स्तर पर मौसम में बदलाव देखने को मिल सकता है।
पठानकोट में सबसे कम तापमान, चंडीगढ़ में 13.5 डिग्री
तापमान के आंकड़ों के अनुसार, पठानकोट के मौसम केंद्र में न्यूनतम तापमान 11.3 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया, जबकि शहर में यह 12 डिग्री रहा। लुधियाना और फरीदकोट में रात का तापमान 12.8 डिग्री सेल्सियस रिकॉर्ड किया गया।
वहीं, चंडीगढ़ में न्यूनतम तापमान 13.5 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहा। चंडीगढ़ एयरपोर्ट पर पारा 13.4 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया। इन आंकड़ों से साफ है कि राज्य में रात के समय ठंड का असर धीरे-धीरे बढ़ रहा है।
बलोवाल सौंखड़ी में सबसे ज्यादा 2.3 डिग्री की गिरावट
राज्य के अन्य शहरों की बात करें तो बठिंडा में न्यूनतम तापमान 13.6 डिग्री, अमृतसर में 13.8 डिग्री और पटियाला में 14.1 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया। पिछले 24 घंटों के दौरान बलोवाल सौंखड़ी में तापमान में सबसे अधिक 2.3 डिग्री सेल्सियस की गिरावट आई।
इसके अलावा बठिंडा में न्यूनतम तापमान 1.8 डिग्री और होशियारपुर में 1.6 डिग्री सेल्सियस नीचे आया। कई शहरों में पारे में आई गिरावट से सुबह और रात के समय ठंड का अहसास बढ़ने लगा है।
अगले पांच दिन तापमान में बड़े बदलाव के आसार नहीं
मौसम विभाग के अनुसार, आने वाले पांच दिनों तक दिन और रात के तापमान में किसी बड़े उतार-चढ़ाव की संभावना नहीं है। हालांकि, 12 नवंबर से कुछ इलाकों में बारिश हो सकती है। ऐसे में मौसम का मिजाज स्थानीय स्तर पर बदल सकता है।

नई दिल्ली
दुनिया 2026 को रिकॉर्ड पर दूसरा सबसे गर्म साल बनाने की राह पर है. यूरोपीय संघ की जलवायु निगरानी एजेंसी कॉपरनिकस क्लाइमेट चेंज सर्विस ने शुक्रवार को यह चेतावनी दी. एजेंसी के अनुसार इस साल असामान्य रूप से तेज अल-नीनो पैटर्न इंसानों द्वारा पैदा की जा रही वैश्विक गर्मी को और बढ़ा रहा है।
अब भी 20 प्रतिशत संभावना है कि 2026, 2024 के सबसे गर्म साल के रिकॉर्ड की बराबरी कर ले या उसे पार कर जाए. कॉपरनिकस ने कहा कि वैश्विक तापमान 2026 में प्री-इंडस्ट्रियल स्तर से 1.5 डिग्री सेल्सियस ऊपर जाना अब लगभग तय हो चुका है. 2023 से 2026 तक का चार साल का औसत भी 1.5 डिग्री पार कर जाएगा।
पेरिस समझौते में सबसे खराब असर रोकने के लिए यही सीमा तय की गई थी. अक्टूबर इस साल का सबसे गर्म अक्टूबर साबित हुआ. वैश्विक सतह हवा का औसत तापमान प्री-इंडस्ट्रियल काल (1850-1900) से 1.75 डिग्री अधिक रहा. यह लगातार तीसरा महीना है जब तापमान 1.5 डिग्री से ऊपर रहा।
यूरोपीय सेंटर फॉर मीडियम-रेंज वेदर फोरकास्ट्स की सैमान्था बर्गेस ने कहा कि अक्टूबर ने भी असाधारण गर्मी का सिलसिला जारी रखा. वैश्विक और समुद्री सतह दोनों के तापमान रिकॉर्ड स्तर पर रहे. उन्होंने बताया कि बेहद तेज अल-नीनो मानवीय गतिविधियों से पहले से गर्म हो चुकी जलवायु में और गर्मी जोड़ रहा है।
अल-नीनो अभी चरम पर नहीं पहुंचा
वैश्विक पूर्वानुमानकर्ता कई महीनों से चेतावनी दे रहे हैं कि यह अल-नीनो इस साल के अंत में चरम पर पहुंचकर अब तक का सबसे तेज बन सकता है. पिछले महीने प्रशांत महासागर के एक प्रमुख क्षेत्र में तापमान ने सर्वकालिक रिकॉर्ड तोड़ दिया. अल-नीनो प्राकृतिक जलवायु चक्र का गर्म चरण है।
यह उष्णकटिबंधीय प्रशांत में समुद्र का तापमान बढ़ाता है जिससे मौसम में बदलाव आता है. सूखा और बाढ़ का खतरा बढ़ता है और मानव जनित गर्मी और तेज हो जाती है. पूर्वानुमान है कि अल-नीनो की वजह से 2027 सबसे गर्म साल बन सकता है।
यह रिपोर्ट ऐसे समय आई है जब देश सोमवार से तुर्की में संयुक्त राष्ट्र के दो हफ्ते लंबे COP31 जलवायु सम्मेलन के लिए तैयार हो रहे हैं. इस साल नेपाल में जानलेवा बाढ़, यूरोप में भीषण गर्मी की लहरें और इंडोनेशिया में बड़े जंगली आग जैसी घटनाएं हुईं।
2015 के पेरिस समझौते में देशों ने वैश्विक गर्मी को प्री-इंडस्ट्रियल स्तर से 2 डिग्री से काफी नीचे रखने और 1.5 डिग्री तक सीमित रखने का लक्ष्य रखा था. लेकिन संयुक्त राष्ट्र ने सितंबर में ही कह दिया था कि लंबी अवधि का 1.5 डिग्री लक्ष्य कुछ सालों में चूक जाएगा।
वैज्ञानिकों का कहना है कि जीवाश्म ईंधन से होने वाली ग्रीनहाउस गैस उत्सर्जन कम करना जरूरी है ताकि 1.5 डिग्री से ऊपर का समय कम से कम रहे और तापमान जल्द नीचे लाया जा सके. कॉपरनिकस की यह चेतावनी साफ संकेत है कि गर्मी का सिलसिला थमने का नाम नहीं ले रहा।

भोपाल(ईन्यूज एमपी)- मध्यप्रदेश में अब ठंड का असर धीरे-धीरे बढ़ने लगा है। प्रदेश के 17 शहरों में न्यूनतम तापमान 15 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे पहुंच गया है। अमरकंटक और कटनी के करौंदी में रात का तापमान 12 डिग्री से भी कम दर्ज किया गया। वहीं, सीधी जिले में न्यूनतम तापमान 14.8 डिग्री सेल्सियस रिकॉर्ड किया गया है। मौसम विभाग ने आगामी चार दिनों में न्यूनतम तापमान में 1 से 2 डिग्री तक गिरावट होने की संभावना जताई है।

articles.full_text:
British heatwaves and massive, thick dwarven beards, perhaps unsurprisingly, don’t mix well together.
We’re inside a soundstage at Shepperton Studios in late June for Season 3 of Prime Video’s “The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power,” and with mercury levels topping 90 degrees and wildfire alerts across Greater London, the residents of the dwarf kingdom of Khazad-dûm are facing a dastardly new villain: sweat.
But help is at hand, literally. Almost every cast and crew member, numbering in the hundreds, is holding a mini fan. If a fan isn’t spotted in the back of a shot (remember the “Game of Thrones” coffee cup?), it’ll be a miracle.
Cameras are getting ready to roll, and before Owain Arthur — who plays newly crowned dwarf King Durin IV — steps onto a set that looks like it been carved out of the Misty Mountains themselves, one assistant holds a mini fan directly in front his face while another points one at the back of his neck.
For all the valiant efforts, the battle against the intense heat isn’t always victorious.
“Eddie Marsan’s beard suddenly peeled off in a close-up yesterday,” notes hair and make-up designer Flora Moody. “We’re really try to keep things on, but it’s a struggle — everyone’s just sweating so much.”
While few may have foreseen an early summer heatwave such as this, Moody hasn’t exactly helped matters. To reflect Season 3 jumping ahead five years after Season 2, she upped the volume of on-screen hair considerably.
“I think this is one of the hairiest shows,” she suggests. As a result, the dwarf beards — made of yak tail hair (quite itchy, apparently) — are bulkier, longer and often more elaborate plaited. Crucially, they’re heavier, so when the glue holding them in place mixes with sweat, they are more liable to slip off.
It’s not any easier for the prosthetics team, which is desperately trying to stop the same fate as Marsan’s beard happening to their oversized dwarven noses and ears.
“When you’re getting somebody into a thick layer of rubber and then covering them in really heavy leather costumes, they’re just walking saunas,” says Barrie Gower, who, alongside his wife Sarah Gower, has overseen the creation of the thousands of body parts being used across the show. “We’re probably one of the most irritating departments for the actors and supporting artists, because we spend the entire day walking around and prodding their faces to try to preventing things from peeling off them.”
Inside Khazad-dûm, more elaborate dwarven cooling technologies have also been deployed.
“We had ice vests,” notes Marsan, speaking after the shoot. The veteran actor joins “Rings of Power” Season three as Thrain — a power-hungry dwarf looking to claim the throne from his younger brother Durin IV (who was only given it following the climactic finale of Season 2, when his dad sacrificed himself to keep a balrog at bay).
Powered by battery, the thin ice vests “have water channels, a little bit like an electric blanket,” says costume designer Libby Dempster, upped to lead for Season 3 and also part of the fight to hold back sweat. “You plug them in between takes and they’re attached to an ice pack.”
But, of course, ice packs didn’t prevent Marsan’s beard-slip moment.
A short electric buggy ride away outside another soundstage, a group of orcs — fully kitted out in scraggly armor, prosthetic faces and terrifying fake eyes are fanning themselves under a tiny amount of shade. Asked how they’re coping, one — almost scripted — bellows: “It’s hotter than the fiery pits of Mordor!”
The heatwave is, of course, being felt across the whole of Middle-earth. But the elves — less weighed down by volumous hair and with wardrobes not so focussed on bulk — aren’t facing quite the same issue. “We didn’t suffer as much as others,” notes Morfydd Clark, who plays Galadriel, after the shoot. However, she says the costume department did find it tricky to “keep the elves looking effortlessly cool while we’re all a bit a sweaty and red.”
That said, Robert Aramayo, playing Elrond, got away with it almost entirely. “He’s the luckiest of the elves, because he doesn’t have a wig,” Clark notes with a comic twang of jealousy. “He just has such a gorgeous natural head of hair.”
Heat — unplanned or not — is something of a theme for “The Rings of Power” Season 3, where over in the fiery volcano of Mount Doom arguably the most seismic event in Tolkien’s entire universe is taking place.
Yes, it’s the forging of the One Ring to Rule Them All by the Dark Lord Sauron himself. As showrunner J.D. Payne says, it’s a hotly anticipated moment that allows Charlie Vickers, having spent the previous two seasons in disguise as Halbrand and Annatar, to finally make his grand long-in-the-works entrance as “full metal Sauron” (with a fancy new sword, too).
Of course, such a momentous occasion — one that will shift the entire story of the series (and, you know, potentially play a part in future plotlines involving Hobbitses) wasn’t one where the filmmakers wanted to go minimal. Fellow “Rings of Power” co-showrunner Patrick McKay describes the ring-making scene they shot as “the most extraordinarily technically complicated sequence we’ve ever attempted on the show,” one that even VFX specialist Jason Smith (an Oscar nominee for the bear sequences on “The Revenant”) said was one of the most complex of his career.
And yet, perhaps offsetting some of this lava-enhanced lurch towards evil, a very different sort of heat is steaming things up elsewhere.
Payne admits that Galadriel has “been through the ringer” so far in “The Rings of Power,” so this time around they’re brightening things up for her with a splash of romance. “From the very beginning, we had a plan to bring back her long-lost husband, who she believes is dead, and this was the season to tell that love story,” he says.
“It’s just lush,” says Clark, adding that it was nice to take a break from the battlefield to spend some time in the “magical fairy realm.”
And in Jamie Campbell Bower, who plays her returning spouse Celeborn (found after a six-month casting process), she says the show has “managed to find an actual real-life elf.”
Things may be looking for Galadriel in Season 3 (aside from the whole Sauron thing, of course) but it’s about to get worse for poor Elrond. The showrunners previously stated that they planned to “break” the youthful, ambitious diplomat seen so far to set him on the path towards the stoic, battle-hardened leader as depicted in the films, and it looks like that’s happening this time.
“They’re constantly testing him — all the time he’s morally grappling with the challenges they’re giving him,” says Aramayo.
The first season of “The Rings of Power” shot during lockdown in New Zealand, arguably the closest country to Middle-earth thanks to Peter Jackson’s efforts. But it shifted to the U.K. — home to a good number of the main cast and heads of department — for the second, mostly divided between Bovingdon Airfield and Bray Studios (which Amazon later acquired and — if rumors are correct — was recently used to hold the final James Bond auditions).
For Season 3, they’ve shifted the entire operation into the newly-expanded Shepperton Studios (which wasn’t ready for Season 2), taking over nine of the 17 new soundstages and a backlot. Funnily enough, Netflix had already moved into the other eight, which it uses to house “Bridgerton” (a mere white fence divides too very different shows).
It’s a hugely impressive setup here. And it’s one, given the worlds and characters being created, that offers some truly wonderful visual moments. Witnessing a group of orcs tuck into craft services (an impressive selection of dishes with each listed on a board alongside their carbon footprint) is a sight that should never get old.
Barring some major upheaval, there won’t be any further relocating. “Season 3 and going forward, we are all in Shepperton,” says McKay. But the vast size and scope of the facility the series now calls home does mean that almost everything can be shot there.
“I think the biggest thing for this season is that we’re not going to go abroad and shoot big foreign landscapes, we’re going to do a lot more here,” says production designer Kristian Milstead, who notes that, while while some of the set builds for Season 3 might not be the biggest on the show, one is certainly the most immersive, allowing for camera shots in all directions (and thus drastically reducing the need for any extension into VFX).
For all the impressive creativity — and creative cooling methods — there is a small oliphaunt in the room.
The “Rings of Power” is widely considered to be the most expensive TV show ever produced, with a reported price tag in the region of $1 billion, way above the likes of “House of the Dragon” or “Stranger Things.”
And yet, despite the record-breaking investment, it hasn’t quite left the cultural mark on the world the team behind it — nor Jeff Bezos himself — might have hoped for. Alongside middling reviews and a backlash from some Tolkien fans, audience numbers have dwindled since its impressive launch (Season 2 had a 60% drop off from Season 1).
“I think with anyone who is shepherding a title or piece of IP with a huge global audience, you have to be your own harshest critic,” says Payne when asked about dealing with exterior noise. “The pressure we put on ourselves as fans of this material — that has been be the God we pray to.”
Given the cost and reaction, there has been questions over whether Prime Video will continue “The Rings of Power.” Amazon originally committed to a five-season, 50-episode run, but Season 4 is yet to be officially greenlit, despite rumors it’s shooting in early 2027.
“We’re busily working away in Middle-earth every day,” says McKay diplomatically when asked if he’s confident the show will get the full five-season run. “We just keep going.”
Clark, meanwhile, simply appreciates that shows as bold, elaborate and as “The Rings of Power” are actually being made.
“I just love to be on something creative where there’s a couple of thousand people employed to do it, it’s just wonderful,” she says. “That’s why I’m always so happy when we have another season because the amount of people that are a part of making it is just massive. So I just feel really lucky to be heading back into this world, but also heading back into it with this village that we’ve got.”

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has warned that a heatwave will continue across several parts of the country on Wednesday with persistently high temperatures expected to last until Friday.
The heatwave is expected to affect North West, most parts of the Free State, southern Gauteng and north-eastern parts of the Northern Cape.
SAWS has also issued warnings for extremely high fire danger conditions across several provinces, raising concerns about the potential for veld fires amid the hot and dry weather.
Despite the soaring temperatures, no impact-based severe weather warnings have been issued for Wednesday.
Heatwave to persist until Friday
According to SAWS, North West and the Free State, excluding its south-western parts, will experience persistently high temperatures until Friday.
Southern Gauteng and north-eastern parts of the Northern Cape will also be affected by the heatwave.
Gauteng is expected to experience partly cloudy and warm to hot conditions, with a very high ultraviolet (UVB) sunburn index.
North West will be fine and hot to very hot, becoming partly cloudy in the eastern parts during the afternoon.
Similar conditions are forecast for the Free State, where fine and hot to very hot weather will dominate before clouds develop in the east later in the day.
Extremely high fire danger across several provinces
SAWS has warned of extremely high fire danger conditions over the Northern Cape, eastern parts of North West and the Free State, and north-eastern parts of the Western Cape.
The warning also extends to parts of the South-Western Bushveld in Limpopo.
In the Eastern Cape, the Dr Beyers Naudé, Inxuba Yethemba and Walter Sisulu local municipalities are among the areas expected to experience extremely high fire danger conditions.
The hot and dry conditions could increase the risk of veld fires, particularly in areas with dry vegetation.
Limpopo and Mpumalanga to experience hot conditions
Limpopo is expected to remain fine and hot to very hot, with partly cloudy conditions developing in the south-west during the afternoon.
Mpumalanga will experience fog patches across most parts of the province before conditions become fine and warm to hot.
The extreme western parts of Mpumalanga will experience partly cloudy conditions.
Western Cape and Northern Cape weather
The Northern Cape will experience cloudy conditions with morning fog patches along the coast and adjacent interior.
Elsewhere in the province, conditions will be fine and hot to very hot, although western areas will be warm in places.
Fresh to strong south to south-easterly winds are expected along the coast.
In the Western Cape, partly cloudy to cloudy and cool to warm conditions are forecast for the extreme south-west, spreading along the south coast and adjacent interior from the afternoon.
The remainder of the province will experience fine and hot weather, with a high UVB sunburn index.
Eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal forecast
The Eastern Cape will experience predominantly fine and warm to hot conditions, with very hot temperatures expected in places in the northern parts of the western half.
Cloud cover is expected to increase in southern areas during the late afternoon.
The eastern half of the province will become partly cloudy in places south of the escarpment during the afternoon.
KwaZulu-Natal will experience fine and warm conditions, becoming partly cloudy in the south during the afternoon.
Moderate to fresh northerly to north-easterly winds are expected along the coast, shifting to south-westerly in the south during the afternoon and spreading towards Mtunzini by evening.
The province is also expected to experience an extreme UVB sunburn index, increasing the risk of sunburn during outdoor activities.
Residents in heatwave-affected areas are advised to remain hydrated, limit prolonged exposure to direct sunlight and exercise caution when using open flames in areas experiencing elevated fire danger.

An international research team has developed genetically engineered cyanobacteria capable of sustaining photosynthesis and cell survival under severe heat stress by reinforcing both antioxidant defenses and protein repair machinery. The study, conducted using the model organism Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803, demonstrates that overcoming thermal damage to photosynthetic systems requires simultaneously reducing oxidative stress and preserving the cellular mechanisms that rebuild damaged proteins.
Photosynthesis is the fundamental biological process that enables plants and microalgae to convert sunlight and carbon dioxide into organic compounds, yet it remains exceptionally vulnerable to elevated temperatures. Within the photosynthetic apparatus, photosystem II functions as the vital molecular complex responsible for converting light energy and releasing oxygen. When environmental temperatures surge, photosystem II faces rapid degradation, while the cellular systems designated to repair the complex become disrupted, presenting a major barrier to photosynthetic efficiency during heatwaves.
The investigation was led by Professor Yoshitaka Nishiyama of the Graduate School of Science and Engineering at Saitama University, collaborating with Dr. Pornpan Napaumpaiporn of the University of Turku and Associate Professor Anchalee Sirikhachornkit of Kasetsart University. Published in the journal Plant and Cell Physiology, their experimental work explored the specific molecular interactions that cause photosynthetic failure when cells encounter extreme temperatures beyond their typical physiological thresholds.
In baseline laboratory experiments, the researchers observed that shifting wild-type cyanobacterial cells from their normal growth temperature of 32 degrees Celsius to an elevated 46 degrees Celsius caused an approximate fourfold surge in the production of reactive oxygen species. The team determined that reactive oxygen species generated during photosynthetic electron transport not only accelerated heat-induced structural damage to photosystem II directly, but also actively suppressed the synthesis of replacement proteins required for ongoing repairs.
To counteract this dual mechanism of heat-induced failure, the researchers developed a two-pronged genetic strategy that addressed both oxidative accumulation and protein synthesis vulnerability. They engineered strains of Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 to overproduce two endogenous antioxidant enzymes, namely the superoxide dismutase SodB and the catalase VktA, to scavenge reactive oxygen species. In tandem, the team introduced a modified version of the translation elongation factor EF-Tu, designated C82S, which was engineered to remain resistant to oxidative inactivation under thermal stress.
Laboratory evaluations demonstrated that combining enhanced antioxidant defenses with the modified translation factor yielded significantly greater protection than either intervention applied individually. While the elevated levels of SodB and VktA limited reactive oxygen accumulation and safeguarded the physical structure of photosystem II, the oxidation-resistant EF-Tu factor preserved the translation of D1, an essential structural protein needed to repair damaged photosystem II complexes. Under severe heat stress at 46 degrees Celsius, the doubly enhanced strain maintained D1 protein synthesis at approximately 1.6 times the level recorded in wild-type cells and experienced markedly less decline in overall photosynthetic activity.
The protective impact of this dual-defense mechanism proved equally critical during prolonged thermal exposure. When maintained under continuous cultivation at 40 degrees Celsius, wild-type cyanobacterial cultures suffered severe bleaching and died, whereas the doubly engineered cells continued to survive and actively proliferate. Because the core molecular machinery governing photosynthesis and translation elongation is conserved across photosynthetic organisms, the researchers noted that this strategy could support more stable outdoor microalgae cultivation for biofuels while offering a molecular framework to engineer heat tolerance in major agricultural crops such as rice, wheat, and soybeans.
The experimental findings provide critical insight into a fundamental dilemma in photosynthetic biology: why photosynthetic systems fail when subjected to severe heat stress. Rather than treating thermal inactivation as a single destructive event, the investigation resolved the process into distinct yet mutually reinforcing pathways. While reactive oxygen species generated during photosynthetic electron transport directly accelerate physical damage to photosystem II, they also impose a secondary block by suppressing the translation of the D1 protein needed to rebuild the damaged complex. Because unmitigated oxidative stress incapacitates translation elongation, simply preventing physical breakdown without safeguarding translational capacity leaves cells unable to recover. The success of the dual-engineered strain underscores that thermotolerance in photosynthetic organisms depends fundamentally on coupling oxidative suppression with the preservation of cellular repair functions.
These molecular insights address practical challenges facing industrial biotechnology, where temperature control represents a major operational hurdle. Microalgae are widely cultivated to manufacture biofuels and other valuable biological materials, but outdoor cultivation facilities are routinely exposed to elevated summer temperatures that impair photosynthetic productivity. In such commercial settings, maintaining optimal thermal conditions typically demands substantial energy inputs for cooling systems. A systematic review and meta-analysis assessing more than five million participants indicates that prenatal exposure to high ambient temperatures, particularly the recurring frequency of extreme heat events, increases the risk of congenital heart defects in offspring. Evaluating pooled epidemiological data from seven studies comprising 5,138,948 participants, including 330,166 documented cases of congenital heart defects, researchers investigated how maternal exposure to extreme thermal conditions during pregnancy relates to structural birth anomalies. The quantitative synthesis demonstrated that the frequency of extreme heat episodes was consistently linked to elevated risk estimates, whereas the recorded duration of these heat events showed no statistically significant association with congenital heart defect outcomes.
Congenital heart defects represent a major global health concern among birth anomalies, prompting ongoing scientific interest in identifying maternal environmental exposures that may influence fetal development during pregnancy. Prior investigations had explored the potential relationship between prenatal heat exposure and the subsequent diagnosis of congenital heart defects in newborns; however, the empirical findings across earlier published studies remained inconclusive. To address these unresolved discrepancies and determine whether maternal thermal stress presents an identifiable risk to cardiac formation, the meta-analysis synthesized data across eligible studies to generate comprehensive summary risk estimates.
To capture the available evidence on maternal heat exposure and fetal cardiac outcomes, the investigators conducted an extensive literature search across four primary bibliographic databases: PubMed, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Embase. The literature search was carried out comprehensively for research published up to February 7, 2025. Following systematic screening according to established inclusion criteria, the authors identified seven independent observational studies that met all methodological standards, yielding a total combined sample of 5,138,948 participants, within which 330,166 cases of congenital heart defects were analyzed.
Exposure assessment within the systematic review encompassed multiple distinct metrics, evaluating both discrete extreme heat episodes and continuous indicators of temperature exposure. Extreme heat events were defined by establishing specific statistical cutoffs based on daily maximum temperatures: periods exceeding the 90th percentile were categorized as EHE90, while periods exceeding the 95th percentile were categorized as EHE95. Continuous exposure was evaluated by measuring the impact of each additional extreme heat event. To calculate pooled associations across the included studies, the investigators employed random-effects models executed in Stata SE15. Summary risk estimates were determined across two analytical criteria: the incremental risk per additional extreme heat event, and the comparative risk between high and low exposure categories.
When extreme heat events were evaluated as binary exposures comparing higher exposure levels against lower exposure levels, the analytical models revealed an overarching positive trend. Within this binary framework, maternal exposure to EHE90 conditions was not significantly associated with congenital heart defect risk. In contrast, a borderline statistically significant association was detected for the more extreme EHE95 threshold, which yielded a pooled relative risk of 1.14 with a 95 percent confidence interval ranging from 1.00 to 1.30. The researchers noted that this borderline significant result for EHE95 indicates an increased risk of congenital heart defects when maternal exposure reaches more extreme temperature thresholds.
Continuous exposure analyses provided further evidence regarding the specific contribution of heat frequency, demonstrating that each additional extreme heat event increased the risk of offspring congenital heart defects. Specifically, each additional EHE90 event was associated with a 3 percent increase in risk, yielding a relative risk of 1.03 with a 95 percent confidence interval between 1.02 and 1.04. Similarly, each additional EHE95 event increased the risk by 4 percent, producing a relative risk of 1.04 with a 95 percent confidence interval between 1.03 and 1.05. In contrast to event frequency, the physical duration of extreme heat events was not significantly associated with congenital heart defect risk. The authors concluded that prenatal exposure to high temperatures, particularly the frequency of extreme heat events, increases offspring congenital heart defect risk, underscoring the critical importance of public health strategies to mitigate heat exposure during pregnancy.

Trans Kalahari Corridor Secretariat to host El Niño heat wave awareness campaign
The Trans Kalahari Corridor Secretariat (TKCS), in partnership with South Africa’s Border Management Authority (BMA), will host a multi-agency El Niño Awareness and Health Screening Campaign on Friday at the Skilpadshek Port of Entry.
The targeted outreach initiative aims to educate cross-border commercial drivers, commuters, and logistics operators on managing extreme heat risks associated with the ongoing El Niño weather pattern.
Meteorologists have warned of extreme heat due to the El Niño climate pattern.
Extreme heat can make every aspect of haulage very demanding, from long hours behind the wheel and at the border to the strain placed on trucks. High temperatures may affect everything from driver health to vehicle performance, increasing the risk of delays, breakdowns and safety challenges.
The TKC borders between Botswana and South Africa have of late been experiencing high traffic volumes due to the increase in cargo and the deviation of traffic from both Groblersbrug / Martins Drift and Beitbridge Border Posts. This has resulted in long queues as well as delays.
It is in this regard that the TKCS is collaborating with the BMA and other key stakeholders to conduct a campaign on El Niño Awareness to sensitize truck drivers on the heatwave, the consequences of the heatwave, and what truckers may do to protect themselves.
The campaign will be held on Friday at Skilpadshek Border Post. The event will feature addresses by the TKCS Executive Director and health professionals, alongside interactive sessions with truck drivers to educate them on heatwaves and their impact on both drivers and equipment.
Health experts and industry partners will train truck drivers on spotting heat stroke symptoms, managing hot weather, tire pressure, preventing equipment strain, and protecting temperature-
sensitive cargo. Free health screenings will also be available for truck drivers and transit commuters. These include vital sign checks, health risk assessments, and on-the-spot nutrition tips for staying safe in extreme heat.
To promote driver wellness, TKCS advises drinking water consistently throughout the day rather than waiting until thirsty, while avoiding caffeine and high-sugar drinks.
Monitor closely for indicators of heat-related illness such as dizziness, profuse perspiration (sweating), nausea, and head pain, and seek immediate medical assistance should they arise. Drivers are also encouraged to use shaded waiting areas, keep their cabs ventilated, and wear lightweight, light coloured clothing and a hat when outside their trucks. Drivers are also encouraged to consume light, easily digestible meals, steer clear of warm or calorie-dense foods that elevate metabolic heat, and utilize available complimentary medical screening for early detection of heat-related conditions.
“The wellbeing of truck drivers and motorists is central to road safety, and through this campaign, we want drivers to have access to practical information and health screenings that help them protect themselves in extreme heat. We encourage every driver passing through Skilpadshek border post to take part and share these messages with fellow drivers.” Executive Director of the Trans Kalahari Corridor Secretariat Leslie Mlungisi Mpofu commented.
He further mentioned that the Secretariat is planning to roll out this important campaign to other areas along the corridor.
The TKC Secretariat is a tripartite trans boundary corridor management institution based in Windhoek. It was established with a political and economic vision to pursue and contribute to deeper regional integration of SADC, SACU, and AUDA -NEPAD.

Drones over Lithuania trigger red alert, NATO jets scrambled but none shot down
Lithuania declared two air alerts overnight, the second red, over drones from Belarus. NATO jets scrambled twice, nothing was shot down, and Vilnius and Kaunas airports closed.
Lithuania declared two air alerts overnight between November 10 and 11, the second at the red level, over drones detected along the Belarus border. NATO fighters from the Baltic air-policing mission took off both times and shot nothing down, while the airports in Vilnius and Kaunas closed their airspace.
Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia have no fighter jets of their own. Allies supply them on a rotating basis, flying out of Šiauliai (in northern Lithuania) and Ämari (in Estonia). That mission, known as Baltic Air Policing, kicks in whenever an unidentified object approaches the border. Alerts in Lithuania are run by the National Crisis Management Centre (NKVC), headed by Vilmantas Vitkauskas, who supplied the account of the night.
What happened overnight
At 21:30 on Tuesday (19:30 GMT) Lithuanian authorities received a warning about possible weather balloons able to disrupt air traffic. Around 23:00 the first yellow alert went out for the Vilnius and Utena regions, lifted shortly after midnight, according to public broadcaster LRT's account.
A second one followed. It started in the Alytus area, spread across much of the center and north of the country and moved from yellow to red, meaning from a precautionary warning to an order to take shelter. Affected areas included Druskininkai, Lazdijai, Marijampolė and Kaunas, along with the districts of Panevėžys, Radviliškis, Pasvalys and Biržai. After 3 a.m. the Latvian army also issued a threat warning for the airspace of the municipalities of Cēsis, Smiltene and Gulbene.
How many drones, and from where
The number needs pinning down right away, because the official accounts show no sign of a swarm. Vitkauskas spoke of three drones detected in Belarus during the first phase, none of which had yet entered Lithuanian territory. In the first episode one drone reportedly ended up in Latvia before heading toward northern Russia.
In the second, a single drone reportedly entered Lithuania from Belarus near Druskininkai, with a possible brief incursion into Poland. It then reportedly worked its way north across the Marijampolė, Kaunas and Panevėžys regions, leaving Lithuanian airspace near Pasvalys. How many there really were, and whether any came down or was hit, remains unclear for now.
NATO jets in the air, no shootdown
Fighters were scrambled in both episodes. They spotted the object without hitting it. Vitkauskas said they came fairly close to making contact, suggesting that bad weather or a position where downing the drone would have endangered people on the ground held them back. Which aircraft took off, and from which base, was not specified.
Šiauliai is, however, the base from which Italian Typhoons destroyed a drone between Kaunas and Kaišiadorys on the night of September 15, the first one downed over Lithuanian territory. That precedent shows the jets can fire when conditions allow. Tonight they didn't find them.
The weak point sits upstream of the fighter, in the radar network. Back in May LRT itself explained that Lithuania's radars can't see low-flying objects and that its air-defense batteries aren't designed for drones. The issue is an industrial one too, as the acquisition of compact-radar maker Echodyne by Shield AI for $5.3 billion shows.
Latvia, Estonia and Poland
Latvia, for its part, was involved twice, because a drone from the first episode actually entered its territory and because its army issued warnings after 3 a.m. Latvian forces activated interceptor drones and air-defense units, on top of the NATO air-policing fighters. They also spoke of similar warnings issued in some areas of Estonia and Lithuania, according to an account citing Reuters.
Poland shows up in only one place, the presumed path of the second drone. A brief, unconfirmed crossing of the border isn't enough to say Poland was involved. The risk of spillover into neighboring countries is real, but tonight the firm data point concerns Latvia.
Airports closed, flights and passengers
Airspace closed first in Vilnius, then in Kaunas, and shut again when the drones moved in. Preliminary information points to three flights affected in Vilnius, with more than 400 passengers on board. No injuries were reported in the first hours. No damage to people or property has been found, though that could change once checks on the ground are done.
An alert like this costs sleep and flights before anyone knows whether there's a target, and it has happened more than once in Lithuania since May.
Not the first time, and the weak spots show
The Baltic sky never sleeps anymore. On May 20 a suspicious drone coming in from Belarus set off the first alert of this kind and Vilnius airport was shut down with fighters mobilized. LRT later reported shelters found locked and the LT72 alert app crashing, with warnings reaching phones only in Lithuanian. Prime Minister Inga Ruginienė had called the situation "bad, very bad".
Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas had promised, in late May, new radars and interceptor drones, with data cross-checked by artificial intelligence, "within a couple of months". Tonight's reports don't say whether those systems are already in service. One thing stands, though, and it's that the new alert is a stress test.
In the background is the war in Ukraine. Ukrainian drones aimed at Russian targets have already strayed into Baltic and Finnish skies several times, with Moscow accusing Kyiv of using NATO airspace and Kyiv answering that Russian electronic warfare diverts some of them. On the other side of the front, as we saw with Kyiv's electronic dome against Shaheds or with the three Yandex data centers hit in four days, drones are now an everyday weapon on both sides. And air-raid warnings are a target too, as the hack on the alert apps in Russia and Ukraine showed.
Frequently asked questions
1. What's the difference between a yellow and a red alert in Lithuania?
Yellow signals a probable air threat, red indicates an air threat in progress. Under red, people in the named areas must take shelter, while yellow is an advance warning. Tonight the second alert started yellow and went red as it spread from the Alytus area to the center and north of the country.
2. What should people in Lithuania do when the alarm sounds?
Follow the instruction for the alert level, and under red head for a shelter. Authorities use the LT72 app and, when the app doesn't work, phone messages. In May the warnings came only in Lithuanian, so a tourist needs a local or hotel staff to translate.
3. Are flights to Vilnius and Kaunas at risk?
Closures last as long as the alert, then airspace reopens. Tonight three flights were affected in Vilnius. Anyone with a ticket in the coming hours would do well to check flight status with the airline before heading to the airport.
4. Does Article 5 of the NATO Treaty apply?
No, because Article 5 covers an armed attack against an ally and no source describes tonight in those terms. There's no indication a drone hit a target. The origin of the objects hasn't been established.
A night to file away, or maybe not
Zero shootdowns, two alerts, two airports at a standstill. On paper the toll looks modest, but the repetition weighs, and Vilnius is getting used to alerts. Getting used to them is, frankly, the real problem. The answer for now is the usual one, wait for the drone to leave the country on its own. A defense that works best in fair weather.
Pressure on the eastern flank isn't only in the air. In the same week fighters were rising over the Baltic, ESET researchers described Turla's Cereal malware on Exchange servers, another face of the same pressure.
